result.title: Imitation Holds a Key to Evolution: Localized Repair and Verified Skill Acquisition for Adaptive Agents
result.summary: An agent can retain successful trajectories without learning which part of an experience should repair a new discrepancy. We formulate passive imitation (PI) as an architectural loop that localizes a violated contract, extracts a local goal, proposes an effect-matched skill, tests a small patch, and retains evidence after full-task verification. We instantiate this loop as a deterministic symbolic controller and analyze its finite repair-query complexity under explicit identifiability and noninterference assumptions. Across ten simulated tool worlds, PI solves all 600 cold held-out composition tasks with three allowed small trials, compared with 6.17% for a whole-trajectory control, while an equally expressive compositional repair control matches PI. On an unseen tool revision, PI achieves 70.0% success versus 24.0% without small trials and 79.0% with self-trial enumeration; an exploratory 24-task adaptation stream subsequently raises first-submission success to 100%, supporting a limited correction-and-retention mechanism rather than a unique incentive advantage or general intelligence. The CPU-only implementation, integrity checks, and reproducible results are available at https://github.com/FriendOfYishan/PI.

AI.brief_summary: 论文把「被动模仿」形式化为一个循环：定位被违反的契约、提取局部目标、提出效果匹配的技能、测试小补丁，并在全任务验证后保留证据；作者以确定性符号控制器实例化该循环，在十个模拟工具环境中分析其修复查询复杂度并做对照实验。
AI.relevance_reason: 「定位需修复的局部经验、小规模试探后经验证再保留」这一机制可能与 LVR 的轨迹训练贡献分配、视觉证据筛选及停止/验证决策有关，可供核查；但该工作为符号化工具环境，无视觉或多模态状态，联系属方法层面的推测。
